learn.hook: Can one child clean a whole muddy path? Maybe not. But what about four children?
points: The lesson 'Together We Can' is about friends who do a big job by working as a team.
Teamwork means people work together to reach one goal.
When everyone does a small part, a big job becomes easy.
To answer a question about a story, find the line that gives the answer.
The title of a story often tells us its main idea.

example.q: Read: The rain had washed mud all over the school path in Mysuru. "It is too much for me," sighed Meera. Then Arjun brought a broom, Salma brought a bucket and Tenzin brought a spade. Everyone took one small job. By lunch, the path was clean. "Alone we are small," smiled their teacher, "but together we can!" Question: How did the children clean the path so quickly?
steps: Look for the line about the work: 'Everyone took one small job.'
So each child did one part of the work.
Many hands together finished the big job fast.
example.answer: They shared the work. Each child did one small job.

learn.reallife: Cleaning the classroom, making a rangoli for a school festival or playing kabaddi: all of these need teamwork.

games.title: Story order
games.prompt: Put the story in the right order
items: Rain washed mud onto the path
Meera sighed that the job was too big
Arjun, Salma and Tenzin brought tools
The path was clean by lunch

games.title: Teamwork: true or false?
items: In a team, everyone can do a part of the job.
When each person does a part, the work gets done faster.
Teamwork means one person does all the work.
Teamwork means many people work together.
Sharing tools is one way to cooperate.
When we share, everyone can help with the job.
Good team members listen to each other.
Listening helps the team agree on a plan.
Laughing at a teammate's mistake helps the team.
Laughing at someone hurts them. Kind words help the team.

quiz.q: Story line: "Arjun brought a broom, Salma brought a bucket and Tenzin brought a spade." What did Salma bring?
quiz.explain: The line says 'Salma brought a bucket'.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up which child brought which tool

quiz.q: Story line: "The rain had washed mud all over the school path." What made the path dirty?
quiz.explain: The rain washed mud onto the path.
quiz.mistake: Guesses instead of reading the line

quiz.q: Meera sighed, "It is too much for me." How did Meera feel at first?
options: Worried that the job was too big
quiz.explain: 'It is too much for me' and a sigh show she felt the job was too big for one person.
quiz.mistake: Does not use the word 'sighed' and the words she said as clues

quiz.q: Story line: "By lunch, the path was clean." When was the path clean?
quiz.explain: The story says the path was clean by lunch.
quiz.mistake: Does not read the time word in the line

quiz.q: The teacher says, "Alone we are small, but together we can!" What does she mean?
options: Small children cannot do any work
It is better to always work alone
Only teachers can do big jobs
We can do big jobs when we work together
quiz.explain: The teacher means that a group working together can do what one person cannot.
quiz.mistake: Takes the word 'small' to mean body size

quiz.q: In "Everyone took one small job," which word tells us that all the children helped?
quiz.explain: 'Everyone' means all the people, so all the children helped.
quiz.mistake: Picks a word without thinking about its meaning

quiz.q: Which is the best title for the story about the muddy school path?
quiz.explain: The story is about friends cleaning the path together, so this title tells the main idea.
quiz.mistake: Chooses a title about one small detail instead of the main idea

quiz.q: Which of these is an example of teamwork?
options: Ravi eats his tiffin by himself
Four friends carry a heavy bench together
quiz.explain: Carrying a bench together means people are working as a team.
quiz.mistake: Does not know that teamwork needs people working together

teach.ask: Gappu wants to build a big nest but it is too hard alone. What is teamwork, and how can it help Gappu?
teach.praise: Yes! When friends work together and each does a part, a big job becomes easy. Gappu will call his friends!
teach.nudge: What happens to a big job when everyone does one part of it?

learn.hook: 'Team' + 'work' makes 'teamwork'. Two small words can join to make a new one!
points: To cooperate means to work together and help each other.
Synonyms are words with the same or nearly the same meaning: help and assist.
Antonyms are words with opposite meanings: together and alone, strong and weak.
A compound word is made of two smaller words: team + work = teamwork, class + mate = classmate.

example.q: Think it through: what is the opposite of 'together' in this sentence? 'We cleaned the room together.'
steps: The opposite would be with no one else.
The word for that is 'alone': 'I cleaned the room alone.'

learn.reallife: When your class plays tug of war, you cooperate with your classmates and pull together.

quiz.q: What does 'cooperate' mean?
quiz.explain: To cooperate is to work together and help each other.
quiz.mistake: Confuses 'cooperate' with a word that sounds similar

quiz.q: Which word means the same as 'help'?
quiz.explain: 'Assist' is a synonym of 'help'.
quiz.mistake: Does not know what a synonym is

quiz.q: Which word is the opposite of 'together'?
quiz.explain: 'Together' means with others; 'alone' means with no one.
quiz.mistake: Picks a word with the same meaning instead of the opposite

quiz.q: Which two words join to make 'teamwork'?
quiz.explain: teamwork = team + work.
quiz.mistake: Splits the compound word in the wrong place

quiz.q: Which of these is a compound word?
quiz.explain: classmate = class + mate, two smaller words joined together.
quiz.mistake: Thinks any long word is a compound word

quiz.q: Choose the right word: "Riya and Kabir ___ their crayons, so both can colour."
quiz.explain: When they share, both children can use the crayons.
quiz.mistake: Does not read the second part of the sentence

quiz.q: Which word is the opposite of 'strong'?
quiz.explain: 'Weak' is the opposite of 'strong'. The other words mean almost the same as strong.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up synonyms and antonyms

quiz.q: "A big job becomes easy when many people help." Which word is the opposite of 'easy'?
quiz.explain: 'Difficult' means hard, the opposite of easy.
quiz.mistake: Chooses a word that means the same as easy

teach.ask: Gappu heard the word 'cooperate'. What does it mean? Can you tell Gappu a word that is opposite to 'together'?
teach.praise: Super! To cooperate is to work together, and the opposite of together is alone. Gappu learnt two words!
teach.nudge: What does 'cooperate' mean? And what is the opposite of 'together'?

topics.title: Naming words: common, proper and collective nouns

learn.hook: Meera, Mysuru, broom and team are all naming words. What kind of naming word is each?
points: A noun is a naming word. It names a person, place, animal or thing.
A common noun is a general name: girl, city, river, broom.
A proper noun is the special name of one person, place or thing: Meera, Mysuru, Ganga. It begins with a capital letter.
A collective noun names a group: a team of players, a flock of birds, a herd of elephants.
More groups: a swarm of bees, a bunch of grapes, a pack of wolves.

example.q: Think it through: find the nouns in 'A team of girls from Pune won a cup.'
steps: 'team' names a group, so it is a collective noun.
'girls' and 'cup' are general names, so they are common nouns.
'Pune' is the name of one particular city, so it is a proper noun.

learn.reallife: Your school name, your city and your best friend's name are proper nouns. Your school's cricket team is a collective noun!

quiz.q: Which of these is a proper noun?
quiz.explain: Chennai is the name of one particular city, so it is a proper noun.
quiz.mistake: Thinks any place word is a proper noun

quiz.q: Fill in: "A ___ of bees buzzed near the flowers."
quiz.explain: A group of bees is called a swarm.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up collective nouns for different animals

quiz.q: Which word is a collective noun?
quiz.explain: 'Team' names a group of players, so it is a collective noun.
quiz.mistake: Does not know that a collective noun names a group

quiz.q: In "Kabir lives in Shimla," which words are proper nouns?
quiz.explain: Kabir is a person's name and Shimla is a place's name. Both are proper nouns.
quiz.mistake: Picks words that are not naming words

quiz.q: Fill in: "A ___ of elephants crossed the river."
quiz.explain: A group of elephants is a herd.
quiz.mistake: Uses 'flock', which is for birds

quiz.q: In "my cousin lives in agra.", which word is a proper noun that needs a capital letter?
quiz.explain: Agra is the name of a particular city, so it is a proper noun and needs a capital A.
quiz.mistake: Thinks a common noun like 'cousin' needs a capital letter

quiz.q: Which of these is a common noun?
quiz.explain: 'Mango' is a general name for a fruit. The others are special names.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up common and proper nouns

quiz.q: In "a team of players", what does the word 'team' name?
quiz.explain: 'Team' is a collective noun. It names a group.
quiz.mistake: Thinks a collective noun names one thing

teach.ask: Gappu is confused. Meera, girl and team are all nouns, but how are they different?
teach.praise: Brilliant! Meera is a proper noun, girl is a common noun and team is a collective noun for a group. Gappu loves nouns now!
teach.nudge: Which kind of noun names a group? And which one starts with a capital letter?
